title: Disabling `borderless` in a maximized window does not keep it maximized
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.6.3, 4.8.dev7

### System information

Godot v4.6.3.stable - Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS 24.04 on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - AMD Radeon 760M Graphics (radeonsi, phoenix, LLVM 20.1.2, DRM 3.57, 6.8.0-146-generic) - AMD Ryzen 5 7640U w/ Radeon 760M Graphics (12 threads) - 13.45 GiB memory

### Issue description

When I have a window in maximized mode and disable `borderless`, it gets smaller (~10-20% if I had to guess).
After enabling and disabling it again, it has the same size as if it would be in windowed mode.
I have a OS scale of 200%, so it ends up 50% smaller overall compared to how it should be.

Possibly somewhat related to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/123994.
That issue is only about `borderless`, this one is about the combination with maximized.

### Steps to reproduce

- set window mode to `maximized`, and `borderless` to `true`
- set `borderless` to `false` => window is no longer maximized
- optional: set `borderless` to `true` and then to `false` again

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A

---

Updated to still be reproducible in 4.8.dev7 before someone asks, just tested it.

---

Update 2:
It seems it just outright changes the window mode to windowed in 4.8.dev7.
Confirmed by printing it after changing `borderless`.
Same behaviour in 4.6.3.
